clue.text: Where children learn to get on?

definitions.text: Where children learn to get on?

parts.words: Where children learn to get on?
parts.note: to get on can mean to make progress in life or to climb aboard a vehicle; the place meant houses pupils who live in

explanation.surface: A question about the school that teaches youngsters how to succeed in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get on' reads as 'succeed', but the joke is the other sense, to board, as in a school where pupils board.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential school is one where pupils lodge, or board, during term.

clue.text: That famous painter, Mr Chips?

definitions.meaning: a great European artist of the period before about 1800
Mr Chips of Goodbye, Mr Chips is an elderly schoolteacher, a veteran schoolmaster

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a celebrated artist was really the fictional teacher Mr Chips.
explanation.walkthrough: Goodbye, Mr Chips is a novel and film about a long-serving teacher at an English boys' school, so he is a schoolmaster grown old.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-1800 great artist is called this, and an aged teacher is literally a schoolmaster grown old.

clue.text: Watery discharge from space, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is what is spoken, so the word for space is replaced by its sound-alike

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: A medical note on a runny leak coming out of somewhere, as reported.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is the thin mucus that runs from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Represent voters in north like the Brunels, for instance

indicators.note: to re-present is to present again in a new form, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An MP standing up for northern constituents, like the great Victorian engineers did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represent' looks like what an MP does for voters; here it signals rearranging VOTERS, IN and N. The Brunels, father and son, were British engineers who invented tunnelling and shipbuilding methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Isambard Kingdom Brunel and his father Marc were creative engineers who devised new machines and techniques.

clue.text: Little information on blood types in Italy

parts.note: gen is informal British slang for information, a short form
O and A are two of the blood groups

explanation.surface: A scrap of data about blood groups in an Italian setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: GEN placed on OA in a down clue. The definition is loose: a place to be found in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoa is a major port city on the north-west coast of Italy.

clue.text: Revolutionary Broadway musical we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the name of the show stands for a word sounding the same

parts.note: Carousel is the Rodgers and Hammerstein Broadway show

explanation.surface: A ground-breaking stage show on Broadway, so it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests something radical, but it means going round and round: the merry-go-round variant spelling with two Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground roundabout turns in circles, so it is a thing that revolves.

clue.text: Conspirator put out to sea

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or disordered, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plotter is sent off on a voyage as punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Oates invented the Popish Plot of 1678, a fictitious conspiracy against Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Oates was a seventeenth-century English plotter and fabricator of the Popish Plot.

clue.text: Final drink that's signalled by a bell

parts.note: last means final
to lap is to drink with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Last orders at a pub, announced by a ringing bell.
explanation.walkthrough: The bell suggests the pub's last orders; in fact in track races a bell rings as runners begin the final circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: In athletics a bell is rung as runners start their final circuit of the track.

clue.text: Tick means a good grade

definitions.meaning: tick is British slang for buying on account, deferred payment
a merit mark in exams, above a pass

explanation.surface: A check mark on schoolwork signals a high mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Tick suggests a check mark; here it is the British slang 'on tick', meaning bought on account.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying on tick means buying on deferred payment, and a pass with merit is graded with this word.

clue.text: Remove part of gamebird's crest

indicators.note: remove tells us to take the following piece out of the bird's name

parts.note: a partridge is a game bird
taken as written

explanation.surface: Plucking some of the feathers off the tuft on a game bird's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crest' looks like the bird's head feathers, but it is the top of a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A hilltop line, the long narrow top of a range, is a crest.

clue.text: Even flexible degrees give honours

indicators.note: flexible means able to bend into another shape, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

parts.note: rates means degrees or grades, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Even-handed university degrees still earn honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' rearranges EVEN to VENE; 'give' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to pay them great respect, which is to honour them.

clue.text: Tell-tales they are not!

parts.note: plays on the saying that those who have died tell no tales, so they cannot betray secrets

explanation.surface: Insisting someone is no sneak or snitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Based on the saying 'dead men tell no tales': corpses cannot inform on anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpses are silent, so the proverb says they cannot reveal secrets.

clue.text: A short spin around America should wake us up

indicators.note: around says the first piece is wrapped round the name of the country
short means cut off before the end, so the last letter of the word for spin goes

parts.note: a roll is a spin or turn, as of an aircraft
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A quick drive around the States ought to rouse us.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: what should wake us up is a rousing, the noun for being stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stirred from sleep or apathy is the state of being roused.

clue.text: Giant bird on middle of branch

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: middle of takes the central letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A huge bird perched midway along a tree limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: TIT placed on AN, the central pair of 'branch'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were a race of enormous gods, so the word means a colossus.

clue.text: Half-way round, of course

parts.note: a full round of golf has eighteen; halfway is the first or back half of the course

explanation.surface: Seems to say that, naturally, someone is midway through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like 'naturally' but means a golf course: half of an eighteen-hole round.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf round of eighteen is split into two halves, an outward and an inward nine.

clue.text: Lie too much, more than the rest

parts.note: over means more than, as in over fifty
sleep is rest

explanation.surface: Fibbing excessively, more than everybody else does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' reads as telling untruths; here it means staying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in bed beyond the time you meant to rise is to stay asleep too long.

clue.text: Candidates have to question low marks

parts.note: to examine is to question, as a witness
E is a low grade in exams, so Es are low marks

explanation.surface: Applicants must query their poor grades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: People sitting a test are candidates for it.

clue.text: High-spirited Texan, Rube's in trouble

indicators.note: in trouble suggests things have gone awry, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A lively Texan, while Rube has problems.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's of Rube's is no letter: TEXAN plus RUBE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of energy and cheerfulness, lively and buoyant.

clue.text: Compass direction to mark, they say, near Alaska

indicators.note: what they say is spoken, so the words before are replaced by their sound-alike

parts.note: a bearing is a compass direction, and to see is to mark or notice

explanation.surface: Navigation instructions to note a heading close to Alaska.
explanation.walkthrough: BEARING (compass direction) and SEE (to mark, notice) sound like the name of the waters between Siberia and Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern arm of the Pacific lies between Alaska and Siberia.

clue.text: Major part in stage play

parts.note: Major is a military rank in the title of a Shaw play, and the part is its heroine's name

explanation.surface: A leading role in a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major part' looks like a leading role, but Major is the Salvation Army rank in Shaw's play Major Barbara; the title role is the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's play Major Barbara is named for its heroine, a Salvation Army officer.

clue.text: Parasites maintained by public expense — I'm one!

definitions.text: Parasites maintained by public expense — I'm one!

parts.words: Parasites maintained by public expense — I'm one!
parts.note: a scrounger living off public money is called a parasite, and the speaker is a single member of the insect plural lice

explanation.surface: A confession from someone living off the state that they are a sponger.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'Parasites' is lice; the singular, one of them, is the answer, also a word of contempt for a scrounger.
explanation.definitionFit: Lice are blood-sucking insects; a single one, and also a contemptible person, has this name.

clue.text: Is not PC about women, first to last

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter is moved to the end

parts.note: someone prejudiced against women is sexist, not politically correct

explanation.surface: A claim that someone's attitude to women is politically incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the S of SEXIST to the end, giving the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To be, as in 'it is', means to have being, to be present in reality.

clue.text: Diversified, but lacking capital, went into farming

indicators.note: lacking capital means without its capital or first letter

parts.note: a firm that diversifies branches out into new areas

explanation.surface: A business branched out but, short of money, took up agriculture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money, but it is the first letter, B, removed from BRANCHED. 'but' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a large livestock farm, as in the American West, is to ranch.

clue.text: Article upset Robert Clive for example

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
Bob is short for Robert

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece annoyed Robert Clive.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Clive, 'Clive of India', made a fortune in India: a nabob was a European who grew rich there.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive of India was the archetypal rich returnee from India, a wealthy man of this kind.

clue.text: Wild dog welcomed at home? Unlikely!

definitions.text: Wild dog welcomed at home? Unlikely!

indicators.note: welcomed means taken in, so the word for home goes inside
wild means unruly and out of order, so the word dog is rearranged

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Would a wild dog be invited into the house? Hardly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: an Australian wild dog would hardly be welcomed into anyone's house.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian wild dog is hardly a welcome guest, being an untamed predator.

clue.text: Sort of serial, one from Jerusalem perhaps

indicators.note: sort means to arrange, so the letters of serial are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A type of TV serial, possibly from Jerusalem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like 'kind of'; it signals rearranging SERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A person native to the Middle Eastern state containing Jerusalem is so called.

clue.text: Female rambler possibly takes one

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rambler is a climbing rose, one example
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A woman out walking may take a single step.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambler' looks like a hiker, but it is a rambling rose, a climbing kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a girl's name, so it can stand for a female.

clue.text: A doctor needs superior sharp instrument in here, maybe

definitions.text: A doctor needs superior sharp instrument in here, maybe

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
U stands for upper-class or superior, as in U and non-U
a lance is a sharp-pointed weapon

explanation.surface: A doctor requiring a top-quality scalpel, maybe on board.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class is a British convention. 'needs' is a link word; the whole clue suggests a medic working inside an emergency vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A medic may well treat a patient on board the emergency vehicle taking them to hospital.

clue.text: Sting turned out well

definitions.meaning: to sting is to hurt with a sharp pain
well dressed and neat in appearance

explanation.surface: A painful sting that somehow ended happily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out well' looks like 'ended happily', but means well dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound smarts when it hurts sharply, and a neatly dressed person looks chic.

clue.text: Safety precautions for smokers in bed?

definitions.text: Safety precautions for smokers in bed?

parts.words: Safety precautions for smokers in bed?
parts.note: fireproof bedding would protect anyone who lights up under the covers

explanation.surface: A warning about the danger of smoking in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The sheets meant here are fireproof mineral-fibre panels, read as fireproof bed linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire-resistant mineral panels would, in a joke, be bed linen that cannot catch alight.
